title: Ogoma's lemma
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $M$ a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and $S\subset A$ a multiplicative subset, with $S^{-1}M$ the localization of $M$ at $S$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Let $\pi\in A$ and suppose $\operatorname{Ker}(\pi:S^{-1}M\to S^{-1}M)=\operatorname{Ker}(\pi^2:S^{-1}M\to S^{-1}M)$. Then there is $s\in S$ such that for every integer $n>0$, $\operatorname{Ker}(s^n\pi:M\to M)=\operatorname{Ker}((s^n\pi)^2:M\to M)$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07FC (lemma-ogoma, line 2287), Section 07FB

proof.text: Set $K=\operatorname{Ker}(\pi:M\to M)$ and $K'=\{m\in M:\ \pi^2m/1=0\text{ in }S^{-1}M\}$, the preimage of $\operatorname{Ker}(\pi^2:S^{-1}M\to S^{-1}M)$ under the $A$-linear localization map $M\to S^{-1}M$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]; both are $A$-submodules of $M$, and $K\subseteq K'$ since $\pi m=0$ gives $\pi^2m/1=0$. Let $Q=K'/K$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma 07FC (lemma-ogoma), proof, lines 2296-2303

proof.text: Every element of $Q$ is killed by an element of $S$, i.e. $S^{-1}Q=0$ ('by assumption' in Stacks): let $m\in K'$. Multiplication by $\pi$ on $S^{-1}M$ sends $x/t$ to $\pi x/t$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], so $\pi^2(m/1)=\pi^2m/1=0$, i.e. $m/1\in\operatorname{Ker}(\pi^2)=\operatorname{Ker}(\pi)$ on $S^{-1}M$ by hypothesis; hence $\pi m/1=\pi(m/1)=0$, so $t\pi m=0$ for some $t\in S$ (an element $x/1$ is $0$ iff $ux=0$ for some $u\in S$). Thus $\pi(tm)=0$, i.e. $tm\in K$, and $t$ kills the class of $m$ in $Q$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma 07FC (lemma-ogoma), proof, lines 2296-2303

proof.text: $Q$ is a finitely generated $A$-module: $K'$ is a submodule of the finitely generated module $M$ over the Noetherian ring $A$, hence finitely generated [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], and the images in $Q=K'/K$ of finitely many generators of $K'$ generate $Q$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma 07FC (lemma-ogoma), proof, lines 2296-2303

proof.text: By Steps 2 and 3, $Q$ is a finitely generated $A$-module with $S^{-1}Q=0$, so there is $s\in S$ with $sQ=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-localization-zero-annihilator]; that is, $sm\in K$, i.e. $\pi sm=0$, for every $m\in K'$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma 07FC (lemma-ogoma), proof, lines 2296-2303

proof.text: This $s$ works ('Then $s$ works' in Stacks; written out): let $n>0$. If $s^n\pi m=0$ then $(s^n\pi)^2m=s^n\pi(s^n\pi m)=0$, so $\operatorname{Ker}(s^n\pi)\subseteq\operatorname{Ker}((s^n\pi)^2)$. Conversely let $(s^n\pi)^2m=s^{2n}\pi^2m=0$. Then in $S^{-1}M$, $\pi^2m/1=s^{2n}\pi^2m/s^{2n}=0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], so $m\in K'$, and by Step 4 $\pi sm=0$; since $n\ge1$, $s^n\pi m=s^{n-1}(\pi sm)=0$. Hence $\operatorname{Ker}(s^n\pi:M\to M)=\operatorname{Ker}((s^n\pi)^2:M\to M)$ for every $n>0$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma 07FC (lemma-ogoma), proof, lines 2296-2303

split_report.summary: Statement checked against Stacks 07FC (smoothing.tex 2287-2295) and kept; added the citations def-weil-finitely-generated-module and the new definition def-weil-pbc-module-localization (localization of a module at a multiplicative subset, Stacks 07JZ, Mathlib leaf LocalizedModule; the existing def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away covers only S={1,f,f^2,...}). Proof written in five steps following the Stacks proof (K, K', Q=K'/K; S^{-1}Q=0 written out elementwise; Q finite by the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite (Stacks 00IK, Submodule.FG.of_le); s in S with sQ=0 by the new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-localization-zero-annihilator (Stacks Exercise 076A, absent from Mathlib in this generality); 'then s works' written out). The Stacks proof does not use stabilization of kernels of powers, exactness of localization or Artin-Rees, contrary to the guesses in the brief. The citer lem-weil-pbc-popescu-resolve-char-p uses the case n=1, which the statement covers. Mathlib search of the item itself (three kinds) kept as recorded by its creator.
